title: Congruent Figures on a Grid Review
description: Review congruent figures, rigid transformations, corresponding measurements, and non-examples.

questions.questionText: Triangle A has side lengths 3, 4, 5. Which triangle is congruent to Triangle A?
questions.explanation: Congruent triangles have matching corresponding side lengths.

questions.explanation: Congruent triangles have matching corresponding side lengths.

questions.questionText: A rectangle is 6 units by 4 units. Which rectangle is congruent to it?
options: A rectangle that is 6 units by 5 units
A rectangle that is 12 units by 8 units
A rectangle that is 4 units by 6 units
A rectangle that is 5 units by 4 units
questions.correctAnswer: A rectangle that is 4 units by 6 units
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape; stretches and non-unit dilations do not.

questions.questionText: A triangle has angles 40, 60, and 80 degrees and side lengths 5, 7, and 9. Which triangle is congruent?
options: A triangle with angles 80, 40, 60 degrees and side lengths 9, 5, 7
A triangle with angles 40, 60, 80 degrees and side lengths 10, 14, 18
A triangle with angles 45, 55, 80 degrees and side lengths 5, 7, 9
A triangle with angles 40, 60, 80 degrees and side lengths 5, 7, 10
questions.correctAnswer: A triangle with angles 80, 40, 60 degrees and side lengths 9, 5, 7
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape; stretches and non-unit dilations do not.

questions.questionText: Figure A is translated 3 units right and 2 units down to make Figure B. What must be true?
options: Figure B is larger than Figure A.
Figure B is similar but not congruent.
Figure B has different angle measures.
Figure A and Figure B are congruent.
questions.correctAnswer: Figure A and Figure B are congruent.
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape; stretches and non-unit dilations do not.

questions.questionText: Figure A is reflected across the y-axis to make Figure B. What must be true?
options: Corresponding angles are cut in half.
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape; stretches and non-unit dilations do not.

questions.questionText: Figure A is rotated 180 degrees to make Figure B. Which measurement is preserved?
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape; stretches and non-unit dilations do not.

questions.questionText: A shape on a grid is stretched horizontally. Is the image congruent to the original?
options: Yes, because the shape stays on the grid.
No, because a stretch changes distances.
No, because translations are not rigid.
questions.correctAnswer: No, because a stretch changes distances.
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape; stretches and non-unit dilations do not.

questions.questionText: Two grid figures have the same shape but one has all side lengths doubled. What is true?
options: They are similar, but not congruent.
They have different angle measures only.
They are related by a reflection only.
questions.correctAnswer: They are similar, but not congruent.
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape; stretches and non-unit dilations do not.

questions.questionText: Which evidence is strongest for congruence on a grid?
options: Both figures are in Quadrant I.
Both figures have one horizontal side.
Both figures have vertices with integer coordinates.
A sequence of translations, rotations, and reflections maps one figure exactly onto the other.
questions.correctAnswer: A sequence of translations, rotations, and reflections maps one figure exactly onto the other.
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape; stretches and non-unit dilations do not.

options: Only the area of the grid

questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape; stretches and non-unit dilations do not.

questions.questionText: Which transformation can create a congruent image?
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape; stretches and non-unit dilations do not.

questions.questionText: A polygon and its image have matching side lengths, but one angle is different. Are they congruent?
options: Yes, side lengths are enough for every polygon.
Yes, all grid figures are congruent.
No, corresponding angles must also match.
questions.correctAnswer: No, corresponding angles must also match.
